ety.text: Borrowed from Chinese 甘肅 /甘肃 (Gānsù).

Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀘𑀓𑁆𑀓 (cakka) + Middle Indo-Aryan -𑀓- (-ka-) without cluster simplification, from Sanskrit चक्र (cakra), from Proto-Indo-Aryan *ćakrám, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *čakrám, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷékʷlos. Doublet of चाक (cāk), चक्र (cakra), and चर्ख़ (carx); see there for more.
Deverbal form of चुदाना (cudānā) with the suffix -आई (-āī).

ety.text: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *(s)reg-der. Sanskrit रञ्ज् (rañj) Sanskrit रङ्ग (raṅga) Prakrit 𑀭𑀁𑀕 (raṃga) Hindi रंग Inherited from Prakrit 𑀭𑀁𑀕 (raṃga), from Sanskrit रङ्ग (raṅga), which is derived from the root रञ्ज् (rañj). Also influenced by Classical Persian رنگ (rang). In either case, ultimately from Proto-Indo-Iranian *(H)rag-, *(H)ranǰ- (“to dye, color”), of unclear origin. Cognate with Gujarati રંગ (raṅg), Marathi रंग (raṅga), Punjabi ਰੰਗ (raṅg) and Odia ରଙ୍ଗ (raṅga).
Borrowed from Sanskrit वक्रतुण्ड (vakratuṇḍa). By surface analysis, वक्र (vakra, “curved, crooked”) + तुण्ड (tuṇḍ, “trunk, snout, beak”).

s.g: Vakratunda, an epithet of Ganesha, referring to his curved trunk

ety.text: Borrowed from Sanskrit वक्रतुण्ड (vakratuṇḍa). By surface analysis, वक्र (vakra, “curved, crooked”) + तुण्ड (tuṇḍ, “trunk, snout, beak”).
Borrowed from Classical Persian شادیشده (šādī-šuda). By surface analysis, शादी (śādī, “marriage”) + -शुदा (-śudā, “-ed”).
Borrowed from Classical Persian شلوار (šalwār), from Middle Persian šlwʾl (šalwār, “trousers”). Compare Bengali সালোয়ার (śalōẇar).
